sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This species is very close to H. blairi Roonwal and Sen Sarma from the Andaman Islands and to H. nicobarensis from Great Nicobar Island. It differs from H. blairi (soldier) as follows: (1) smaller size; head dark brown, narrower, nasus stouter (the latter larger, head reddish brown, much wider, nasus more slender); (2) segment 3 of the antenna 2.60-2.67 times the length of segment 2 (in the latter not more than 2.40-2.50 times); (3) antennal segments pale yellow, only segments 1 and 2 darker (in the latter all segments darker). For the differences from H. nicobarensis see the account of that species. Type locality: Nancowry, Nicobar Islands; distribution known only from the type locality.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier (Fig. 9a-d): head dark brown, the anterior part (including the nasus) much paler; antennae pale brown; pronotum and abdominal tergites dark brown. Head and pronotum without long hairs; tergites with minute hairs; legs and sternites with long hairs. Body length (excluding antennae, including nasus) 4.10-4.50 mm. Head (without nasus) pyriform, distinctly constricted below the antennal sockets; sides more convex posteriorly; posterior margin broadly rounded. Nasus slender, cylindrical, much longer than half the head length without nasus, apex with a few minute hairs. In lateral view the dorsal margin of head plus nasus is rather incurved; the basal swelling of the nasus very weak; the posterior elevation of the head rather well developed. Frontal gland and frontal tube indistinct. Antennae 14-segmented, the basal 2 segments much darker than the rest; segment 3 about 2.5 times as long as segment 2, only slightly longer than segment 4; segment 2 the smallest; segments 5-8 onwards subequal in length, segments 9-14 gradually shorter. Mandibles highly reduced, each with a spine-like lateral process situated near the middle of the outer margin; the edge between the spine-like process and the molar region straight; the spine much longer than the molar region, which is weakly convex. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, much narrower than the head width; anterior lobe smaller than the posterior lobe, anterior margin weakly convex and with minute hairs, without a median notch; lateral angles narrowly rounded; posterior margin weakly convex, with a very weak median notch; a white median line divides the pronotum into two equal halves. Legs slender; femora strongly chitinised, hind femur longer, reaching the apex of the abdomen; tibial spur formula 2:2:2; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate-oval, posterior margin of each tergite with a few scattered minute hairs. Cerci 2-segmented. Stylus absent. Measurements (mm; holotype first, then the range of 10 specimens): head length including nasus 1.68 (1.64-1.72); head length without nasus 1.13 (1.09-1.15); nasus length 0.55 (0.53-0.58); nasus greatest width 0.21 (0.19-0.24); head least width 0.76 (0.72-0.78); head greatest width 1.00 (0.98-1.02); posterior elevation of the head 0.43 (0.43-0.53); head least height 0.63 (0.58-0.63); head greatest height 0.76 (0.75-0.76); nasus-head index I (nasus length/head length without nasus) 0.43 (0.46-0.53); nasus-head index II (nasus greatest width/head greatest width) 0.21 (0.19-0.24); head elevation index (posterior elevation of the head/head length without nasus) 0.38 (0.38-0.47); cephalic constriction index (head least width/head greatest width) 0.76 (0.73-0.78); head index I (greatest width/head length without nasus) 0.88 (0.85-0.90); head index II (greatest height/head length without nasus) 0.67 (0.65-0.70); head index III (greatest height/greatest width) 0.76 (0.74-0.77); pronotum greatest length 0.38 (0.36-0.38); pronotum greatest width 0.68 (0.63-0.68); pronotal index (length/greatest width) 0.56 (0.55-0.60); hind femur length 1.80 (1.70-1.86); antennal segment 3 length/segment 2 length 2.63 (2.60-2.67); number of antennal segments 14 (14).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head capsule and postclypeus dark brown, labrum paler, antennae pale brown; thorax brown; coxae and femora pale brown; tibiae and tarsi pale yellow; abdominal tergites pale brown, sternites much paler. Cephalic hairs sparse; pronotum with short hairs; tergites sparsely hairy, sternites densely hairy. Head capsule subquadrate, slightly wider than long; Y-suture distinct. Fontanelle covered by a white, translucent, narrow, elongate plate, situated at the junction of the two frontal sutures and slightly depressed. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 about twice the length of segment 2, longer than segment 4; segment 2 the smallest; from segments 5-8 onwards gradually longer, segments 9-15 gradually shorter. Behind the antennal sockets a pair of suboval white spots on each side. Postclypeus inflated, width nearly twice the length, divided into two halves by a deep median line, with a few hairs. Anteclypeus band-like, translucent, hairless. Labrum dome-shaped, much wider than long, with a few long setae. Mandibles stout, pale brown, inner margin much darker. Left mandible with 1 apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth; apical tooth well developed, slightly shorter than marginal tooth 1, slender, finger-like, cutting edge undulate; marginal tooth 2 shorter than marginal tooth 1, well developed, directed posteriorly, triangular, distant from marginal tooth 1; molar plate short. Right mandible also with 1 apical tooth, 2 marginal teeth and a well-developed molar plate; apical tooth slightly shorter than marginal tooth 1, marginal tooth 1 triangular, marginal tooth 2 short, with a long inward-directed cutting edge; molar surface undulate. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, much narrower than the head width, wider than long, anterior margin straight, weakly notched; anterolateral angles deeply concave; posterior margin broadly rounded. Legs long and slender, hind femur extending beyond the apex of the abdomen. Abdomen elongate-oval, posterior margin of each tergite with a row of small hairs. Cerci 2-segmented, stylus absent. Minor worker: slightly smaller than the major worker; head paler, antennae darker; hairs and other characters as in the major worker. Head subquadrate, slightly wider than long; Y-suture distinct; fontanelle as in the major worker. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 2 the shortest, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2 or 4, segments 5-9 gradually longer, segments 10-15 gradually shorter. Postclypeus, anteclypeus, labrum, mandibles, etc. all as in the major worker. Pronotum as in the major worker, but the anterolateral notch very weak. Abdomen as in the major worker. Measurements (mm; major workers 5 specimens, minor workers 5 specimens, in that order): head length to the lateral mandible base 1.09-1.15, 0.86-0.96; head greatest width 1.15-1.18, 1.00-1.09; head greatest height 0.62-0.64, 0.56-0.58; labrum greatest length 0.34-0.35, 0.30-0.34; labrum greatest width 0.45-0.48, 0.46-0.48; pronotum greatest length 0.48-0.50, 0.38; pronotum greatest width 0.76-0.81, 0.65-0.68.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type material: holotype, 1 soldier (Z.S.I. registration no. 3184/H, superscript illegible in the OCR), deposited in the Zoological Survey of India, Calcutta (Z.S.I.); paratypes, 5 soldiers and 6 worker morphotypes (3 major, 3 minor) in one tube (Z.S.I. registration no. 3185/H), deposited in Z.S.I., Calcutta; a further 2 soldiers and 2 worker morphotypes in one tube, deposited in F.R.I., Dehra Dun. All type specimens are in fluid, with the collection data given under "Material".

note: Rewritten from the new-species description of Maiti & Chakraborty (1994); the original is in English. The original records the alate as Unknown, hence there is no section for it; the worker is dimorphic, major and minor. The OCR of the original contains many garbled characters (mu,h, flaveolae, buldging, ergites, comers, Pronntum, veiy, Pn>ntum, etc.), normalised to standard words from context; all figures are reproduced unchanged. In the soldier measurement table the holotype value of "nasus-head index I" is 0.43, below the lower limit of the range 0.46, as in the original. The tibial spur formula, printed in the OCR as 2:2;2, is recorded as 2:2:2.
